draft.title: Natural and farmed ecosystems
card: An ecosystem is the living things in an area and the non-living things they depend on, such as soil, water and sunlight.
A natural biome has many species of plants and animals. Its nutrients are recycled when plants and animals die and rot into the soil, and water cycles through rain, soil and plants.
A farm has far fewer species, often one main crop or animal. People add nutrients such as fertiliser and water, and remove them when they harvest the crop.
Because harvested food leaves the farm, its nutrients do not return to the soil by themselves.
draft.remember: A farm has fewer species, and people control its nutrients and water.

a.q: How does a wheat farm differ from the grassland it replaced?
opts: It has fewer species, and people manage its nutrients
It has more species, and its nutrients cycle naturally
It has fewer species, and its nutrients cycle naturally
It has more species, and people manage its nutrients
a.why: Farms are planted with one main crop, so they have fewer species. Harvesting removes nutrients, so people must manage them. The third option is tempting because it gets the species right, but nutrients no longer cycle naturally.
a.clue: Count the species, then ask who controls the nutrients.

b.q: Priya harvests all the tomatoes from her field each year and carts them to market. Why might her soil run low on nutrients?
opts: Harvesting removes nutrients that do not return naturally
Tomato plants add too many nutrients to the soil
Natural recycling speeds up when crops are harvested
Farm soil never holds any nutrients to begin with
b.why: In a natural ecosystem, dead plants rot into the soil and return nutrients. When crops are carted away, that return stops. The soil does hold nutrients, but harvesting takes them out faster than they come back.
b.clue: Where do the plants go when harvested?

a.best: It has fewer species, and people manage its nutrients

b.best: Harvesting removes nutrients that do not return naturally

'People add nutrients such as fertiliser and water' reads as if water is a nutrient. It should be 'People add nutrients, such as fertiliser, and water' or similar, so water and nutrients are clearly separate inputs.
